sources.title: CDC Yellow Book 2026: High-Altitude Travel and Altitude Illness
sources.use: Current guidance (Hackett and Shlim): acclimatization, the three altitude illnesses, their treatment, the medicines and the hyperbaric bag. With the WMS 2024 guideline, it decides what the game says about medicines.

sources.title: WMS: Acute Altitude Illness Clinical Practice Guideline, 2024 Update, summary
sources.use: The Wilderness Medical Society's own summary of its 2024 guideline, whose full text is behind a paywall: prevention, diagnosis and treatment of AMS, HACE and HAPE, and the AMS classes by Lake Louise score.

sources.title: Omidi et al. 2025, What Is New in Altitude- and Cold-Related Illnesses of Travel (a review of the WMS 2024 guidelines)
sources.use: An open (CC BY) review of the WMS 2024 guidelines on altitude illness, frostbite and avalanche burial: what changed in 2024, with the strength of each recommendation. The game's frostbite and avalanche medicine rests on it.

sources.title: Roach et al. 2018, The 2018 Lake Louise Acute Mountain Sickness Score
sources.use: The consensus score of AMS (CC BY, High Alt Med Biol 19:4–6): four symptoms of 0–3 points, the threshold and the severity classes. The game models a climber's AMS on it; the paper says it's a research tool, not a way to diagnose.

sources.title: UIAA MedCom No 2: Emergency Field Management of AMS, HAPE and HACE (2012, updated 2024)
sources.use: Field management by the UIAA Medical Commission: risk factors, typical altitudes and onset times, the symptoms, what to do on the spot, and what else looks like altitude illness. For symptoms and the order of actions; on medicines, CDC 2026 and WMS 2024 decide.

sources.title: UIAA MedCom No 3: Portable Hyperbaric Chambers (2012)
sources.use: The hyperbaric bag: when to use it and when not, how long a session lasts, the rebound, the pumping, the types and their weights.

sources.title: UIAA MedCom No 10: The Effect of Extremes of Temperature on Drugs (2008)
sources.use: What cold and heat do to the medicines in the kit, and the side effects that matter at altitude: for the first-aid kit's mechanics.

sources.title: UIAA MedCom No 20: Eye Problems on Expeditions (2021)
sources.use: The eyes at altitude: snow blindness, high-altitude retinopathy, loss of vision, contact lenses and eye surgery.

sources.title: UIAA MedCom No 22a: Drug Use and Misuse in Mountaineering (2014)
sources.use: Medicines taken to climb rather than to treat, Everest's included: what each does and risks, and what doesn't work.

sources.title: Medex: Travel at High Altitude (2008 edition)
sources.use: A booklet for trekkers and climbers, recommended by the UIAA: symptoms in plain words, what to do, and real cases. For the game's words and its training scenarios; its score card is the one from before 2018.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Death zone
sources.use: Background on the death zone above 8,000 m, not medical guidance: never a source for a treatment.
